headings: Compensation and Benefits
paragraphs: Founded in 1938 in Portland, Oregon, as a small, family-owned, regional hat distributor and incorporated in Oregon in 1961, Columbia Sportswear Company has grown to become a global leader in designing, developing, marketing, and distributing outdoor, active and lifestyle products, including apparel, footwear, accessories, and equipment.

Unless the context indicates otherwise, the terms "we," "us," "our," "the Company," and "Columbia" refer to Columbia Sportswear Company, together with its wholly owned subsidiaries and entities in which it maintains a controlling financial interest.

We connect active people with their passions by providing them with the products they need to seek inspiration and adventure. We meet the diverse needs of our customers and consumers through our four brands by designing, developing, marketing, and distributing our outdoor, active and lifestyle products, including apparel, footwear, accessories and equipment.

Columbia® | Founded in 1938, our Columbia brand's mission is to unlock the outdoors for everyone. Our Columbia brand offers authentic, high-value outdoor apparel, footwear, accessories and equipment products suited for hiking, trail running, snow sports, and fishing and hunting activities, as well as everyday outdoor activities.

SOREL® | Acquired in 2000, our SOREL brand has evolved from a men's utility boot brand into a contemporary lifestyle brand bringing style to the outdoors. Our SOREL brand leverages its rich heritage, innovation and style to offer distinct, compelling, and unexpected footwear to consumers around the world.

Mountain Hardwear® | Acquired in 2003, our Mountain Hardwear brand's mission is to encourage and equip people to seek wilder paths. With over 30 years of wild wisdom, our Mountain Hardwear brand continues to offer premium technical apparel, accessories and equipment products for climbers, mountaineers, skiers, snowboarders, and trail athletes.

prAna® | Acquired in 2014, our prAna brand's mission is to inspire an active lifestyle, lived with mindfulness and originality. prAna pairs style and functionality to craft versatile apparel and accessories for those who want the freedom to explore ways of moving and being.

Across our diverse portfolio of brands, our products have gained recognition for their innovation, quality, value, and performance. Our products incorporate the cumulative design, fabrication, fit, and construction technologies that we have pioneered over several decades and continue to innovate. Our apparel, accessories and equipment products are designed to be used for all seasons, activities and locations. Our footwear products include durable, lightweight hiking boots, trail running shoes, rugged cold weather boots, sandals, shoes for use in water activities, and footwear for lifestyle wear.

Our business is affected by the general seasonal trends common to the industry, including seasonal weather and discretionary consumer shopping and spending patterns. Our products are marketed on a seasonal basis, and our sales are weighted substantially toward the third and fourth quarters, while our operating costs are more equally distributed throughout the year.

We are committed to designing innovative and functional products for consumers who participate in a wide range of outdoor, active and lifestyle activities, enabling them to enjoy those activities longer and in greater comfort. We distinguish our products in the marketplace through brand-specific product design efforts, with teams focused on aligning product attribute priorities with the needs and preferences of each brand's target consumer, including, but not limited to, product attribute priorities such as versatility, style, quality, value, and technical performance.

Our team of specialists leads both our internal research and development efforts and works closely with independent suppliers to conceive, develop and commercialize innovative technologies and materials to provide the unique performance benefits desired by consumers. We utilize our working relationships with specialists in the fields such as chemistry, biochemistry, engineering, industrial design, materials research, graphic design, and other related fields, along with consumer insights and feedback, to develop and test innovative performance products, processes, packaging, and displays. These efforts, coupled with our drive for continuous improvement, represent key factors in the success of our products.

We seek to substantially limit our invested capital and avoid the costs and risks associated with large production facilities and the associated labor forces; therefore, we do not own, operate or manage manufacturing facilities. The vast majority of our finished goods are produced by contract manufacturers located outside the United States ("U.S."). We establish and maintain long-term relationships with key finished good manufacturing partners, but generally do not maintain formal long-term manufacturing volume commitments. The use of contract manufacturers for our finished goods maximizes our flexibility and historically has benefited our product costs. We continually evaluate our source base and its benefit to our product costs, including evaluation of tariffs and duties.

We value legal, ethical and fair treatment of people involved in manufacturing our products. Independent contractors manufacturing our products are subject to our standards of manufacturing practices to facilitate safe and humane working conditions, as well as to promote ethical business practices. We have programs in place to monitor manufacturer practices and assess alignment with these standards.

headings: Rapidly Evolving U.S. Global Trade Policy Has Had and May Continue to Have an Adverse Impact on Our Business, Operating Results and Financial Condition.
We are Subject to a Number of Risks Which May Adversely Affect Consumer and/or Wholesale Customer Demand for Our Products and Lead to a Decline in Sales and/or Earnings.

Global Regulation and Economic and Political Conditions, as well as Potential Changes in Regulations, Legislation and Government Policy, May Negatively Affect Our Business.

paragraphs: In addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the following risk factors should be considered carefully in evaluating our business. Our business, financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows may be materially adversely affected by these and other risks. Please note that additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business and operations.

Our imported products are subject to duties, tariffs or import limitations that affect the cost and quantity of various types of goods imported into the U.S. and other markets. The changes in U.S. global trade policy, and ongoing uncertainty around future tariffs or other alternative measures and refunds of prior incremental tariffs paid, have had and may continue to have, an adverse impact on our business, financial condition and operating results and may (and in many cases, have):

•Lead to a decline in discretionary spending by consumers weary of inflationary pressures, particularly increased prices for apparel and footwear products in the U.S. (see "We are Subject to a Number of Risks Which May Adversely Affect Consumer and/or Wholesale Customer Demand for Our Products and Lead to a Decline in Sales and/or Earnings");

•Impair the financial health of certain of our wholesale customers (see "We are Subject to a Number of Risks Which May Adversely Affect Consumer and/or Wholesale Customer Demand for Our Products and Lead to a Decline in Sales and/or Earnings");

•Result in a misalignment between demand and supply, as has occurred in our cancellation of product orders in advance of the Fall 2025 and Spring 2026 seasons (see "Our Inability to Accurately Predict Consumer and/or Customer Demand for Our Products Could Lead to a Build-up of Inventory or a Lack of Inventory and Affect Our Gross Margin");

•Impact global economic conditions and contribute to an economic slowdown (see "We are Subject to a Number of Risks Which May Adversely Affect Consumer and/or Wholesale Customer Demand for Our Products and Lead to a Decline in Sales and/or Earnings" and "We May Incur Additional Expenses, Be Unable to Obtain Financing, or Be Unable to Meet Financial Covenants of Our Financing Agreements as a Result of Downturns in the Global Markets");

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements", Item 1, Item 1A, and Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition, refer to Item 7 in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 for our discussion and analysis comparing financial condition and results of operations from 2024 to 2023.

As a global leader in designing, developing, marketing, and distributing outdoor, active and lifestyle products, our mission is to connect active people with their passions. We provide our products through our four brands: Columbia, SOREL, Mountain Hardwear, and prAna; and two major product categories: consisting of apparel, accessories and equipment products, and footwear products. Apparel, accessories and equipment products are provided by our Columbia, Mountain Hardwear and prAna brands. Footwear products are provided by our Columbia and SOREL brands. We sell our products in 115 countries and operate in four geographic segments: U.S., LAAP, EMEA, and Canada.

Our business is affected by the general seasonal trends common to the industry, including seasonal weather and discretionary consumer shopping and spending patterns. Our products are marketed on a seasonal basis, and our sales are weighted substantially toward the third and fourth quarters, while our operating costs are more equally distributed throughout the year.

In 2024, we announced the Columbia brand (the "Brand") ACCELERATE Growth Strategy. At its core, the ACCELERATE Growth Strategy is intended to elevate the Brand to target a younger and more active consumer while maintaining those consumers that have known and trusted Columbia to offer high quality products at an exceptional value. It is a multi-year effort centered around several consumer-centric shifts to the Brand, product and marketplace strategies, as well as enhanced ways of working. We believe successful operationalization of the ACCELERATE Growth Strategy can elevate the Brand and drive profitable growth.

2025 was an important milestone in this journey. The Columbia brand launched its new brand platform "Engineered for Whatever" through a global Brand campaign in print, on social and in-person. The Columbia brand also released certain new products designed with a younger, more active consumer in mind, and re-launched the U.S. Columbia.com website, with enhanced features and photography. We're encouraged with early indicators, which signal that our differentiated marketing communications and enhanced products are resonating with consumers, providing us confidence as we plan for future seasons.
Through the ACCELERATE Growth Strategy, we are focused on achieving the following objectives:
•steward existing consumer segments while focusing on bringing new younger and active consumers into the Brand;
•elevate consumers' perception of the Brand; •create product based on a consumer-centric product construct;
•enhance the positioning of the Brand globally, particularly in the U.S. marketplace; and
•deliver integrated full-funnel marketing.
In addition, we are committed to investing in our company-wide strategic priorities with a renewed emphasis to:
•accelerate profitable growth; •create iconic products that are differentiated, functional and innovative;
•drive brand engagement through increased, focused demand creation investments;
•enhance consumer experiences by investing in capabilities to delight and retain consumers;

paragraphs: 於1938年在俄勒岡州波特蘭成立，為一家小型、家族所有、區域性帽類經銷商，並於1961年在俄勒岡州註冊為公司，Columbia Sportswear Company 已成長為全球領導者，在戶外、活動及生活方式產品的設計、開發、行銷與經銷方面，包括服飾、鞋類、配件與裝備。
除非上下文另有說明，否則「我們」、「我們」、「我們」、「本公司」及「Columbia」一詞均指 Columbia Sportswear Company，包括其全部擁有子公司及本公司擁有控制性財務權益之實體。
我們透過提供產品，讓活躍人羣能追求靈感與冒險。我們透過四大品牌，滿足客戶與消費者多樣化的需求，設計、開發、行銷與經銷戶外、活動及生活方式產品，包括服飾、鞋類、配件與裝備。
Columbia® | 於1938年成立，我們的 Columbia 品牌使命是為所有人解鎖戶外。我們的 Columbia 品牌提供真實、高價值的戶外服飾、鞋類、配件與裝備產品，適合徒步、山徑跑步、雪上運動、釣魚與狩獵活動，以及日常戶外活動。
SOREL® | 於2000年取得，我們的 SOREL 品牌已從一間男性實用靴類品牌，進化為一間現代生活方式品牌，為戶外帶來時尚。我們的 SOREL 品牌運用其豐富的傳統、創新與時尚，為全球消費者提供獨特、吸引人且出人意料的鞋類產品。
Mountain Hardwear® | 於2003年取得，我們的 Mountain Hardwear 品牌使命是鼓勵並裝備人們追求更野性的路徑。擁有超過30年的野外智慧，我們的 Mountain Hardwear 品牌持續提供高階技術服飾、配件與裝備產品，供攀巖者、登山者、滑雪者、單板滑雪者與山徑運動者使用。
prAna® | 於2014年取得，我們的 prAna 品牌使命是激勵活躍的生活方式，並以覺察與原創性來實踐。prAna 結合時尚與功能性，為那些追求自由探索活動與生活方式的人士打造多用途的服飾與配件。
在我們多樣化的品牌組閤中，我們的產品因創新、品質、價值與表現而受到認可。我們的產品 incorporates 我們數十年來所研發的設計、製造、合適性與構造技術，並持續創新。我們的服飾、配件與裝備產品設計為全年、各種活動與地點使用。我們的鞋類產品包括耐用輕便的徒步靴、山徑跑步鞋、堅固的寒冷天氣靴、涼鞋、水活動用鞋，以及生活方式用鞋。
本公司業務受產業普遍存在的季節性趨勢影響，包括季節性天氣與消費者隨意性購物及消費模式。本公司產品以季節性方式進行行銷，銷售額主要集中在第三及第四季，而營運成本則較均勻地分佈於全年。
本公司致力於為參與廣泛戶外、活躍及生活方式活動的消費者設計創新且具功能性的產品，使他們能更長時間、更舒適地享受這些活動。本公司透過品牌特定的產品設計努力，在市場中區分自身產品，並有專案團隊專注於將產品屬性優先順序與各品牌目標消費者的需 求與偏好對應，包括但不限於產品屬性優先順序如多用途性、時尚感、品質、價值與技術性能。
COLUMBIA SPORTSWEAR COMPANY | 2025 FORM 10-K | 1
本公司專門團隊領導內部研究與開發工作，並與獨立供應商密切合作，構思、開發與商業化創新技術與材料，以提供消費者所期望的獨特性能好處。本公司利用與化學、生物化學、工程、工業設計、材料研究、圖形設計及其他相關領域專門人才的業務關係，並結合消費者洞察與意見，開發與測試創新性能產品、流程、包裝與展示。這些努力，加上本公司對持續改進的追求，是本公司產品成功的重要因素。
本公司致力於大幅降低投入資本，並避免與大型生產設施及相關勞動力相關的成本與風險；因此，本公司不擁有、營運或管理製造設施。本公司絕大多數成品由位於美國以外的合同製造商生產（"U.S."). 本公司建立並維持與關鍵成品製造商的長期關係，但通常不維持正式的長期製造量承諾。本公司使用合同製造商生產成品，以最大化靈活性，並歷來有助於產品成本。本公司持續評估來源基地及其對產品成本的效益，包括評估關稅與費用。
本公司重視法律、倫理及對參與製造本公司產品之人士的公平待遇。獨立製造商製造本公司產品時，需遵守本公司製造作業標準，以促進安全與人道的作業環境，並促進倫理商業作法。本公司已建立監測製造商作法的方案，並評估其與這些標準的符合程度。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應配合本年度10-K申報表中「Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements」、第1項、第1A項及第8項一併閱讀。此外，請參閱我們2024年12月31日為結算日之年度10-K申報表第7項，以瞭解我們對2024年與2023年財務狀況及營運成果之比較分析。

作為設計、開發、行銷與分銷戶外、活躍與生活方式產品的全球領導者，我們的使命是將活躍人羣與他們的熱情連結。我們透過四大品牌：Columbia、SOREL、Mountain Hardwear 及 prAna 提供產品；並分為兩大產品類別：包含服飾、配件與裝備產品，以及鞋類產品。服飾、配件與裝備產品由 Columbia、Mountain Hardwear 及 prAna 品牌提供。鞋類產品則由 Columbia 及 SOREL 品牌提供。我們的產品銷售遍及115個國家，並在四大地理區段進行營運：美國、LAAP、EMEA 及加拿大。
我們的業務受產業普遍存在的季節性趨勢影響，包括季節性天氣與消費者自由支配購物與消費模式。我們的產品以季節為基礎進行行銷，銷售收入主要集中在第三及第四季，而營運成本則較均勻地分佈於全年。
2024年，我們宣佈了 Columbia 品牌（「品牌」）ACCELERATE 成長策略。該策略的核心是將品牌提升，以針對較年輕且活躍的消費者，同時維持那些已知且信任 Columbia 提供高品質產品並具有優異價值的消費者。這是一項跨年度的計畫，圍繞品牌、產品與市場策略的多項消費者導向的轉變，以及提升作業方式。我們相信成功落實 ACCELERATE 成長策略，將能提升品牌並推動獲利成長。

2025 是這段旅程中的重要里程碑。Columbia 品牌透過全球品牌活動，在印刷品、社交媒體及實體活動中啟動了其新品牌平台 "Engineered for Whatever"。Columbia 品牌也推出了某些針對年輕、更具活動力消費者設計的新產品，並重新啟動了美國 Columbia.com 網站，並加入增強的功能與攝影。我們對早期的指標感到鼓舞，這些指標顯示我們的差異化行銷溝通與增強後的產品正與消費者產生共鳴，這讓我們在規劃未來季節時更具信心。
透過 ACCELERATE 成長策略，我們專注於實現以下目標：
• 看護現有消費者羣組，同時專注於將年輕且更具活動力的消費者引入品牌；
• 提升消費者對品牌的認知；• 依據以消費者為中心的產品架構開發產品；
•強化品牌在全球的定位，特別是在美國市場；
•提供整合性的全 funnel 營銷。
此外，我們致力於投資本公司整體戰略優先事項，並重新強調：
•加速獲利成長；•創造具有差異化、功能性和創新性的經典產品；
•透過增加、聚焦的 demand creation 投資來推動品牌參與度；
•透過投資能力來提升消費者體驗，以取悅並留住消費者；

headings: 美國快速演進的全球貿易政策已對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生負面影響，並可能持續產生負面影響。
我們面臨許多風險，這些風險可能影響消費者及/或批發客戶對我們產品的需求，導致銷售額及/或獲利下降。
我們若無法準確預測消費者及/或客戶對我們產品的需求，可能會導致存貨積壓或存貨不足，進而影響我們的毛利率。
我們所使用的原材料供應穩定性及價格波動，可能對我們的營收、成本、毛利率及盈利能力產生重大不利影響。
對於某些材料，我們依賴極少數供應商，這可能會導致成本增加或生產延誤。
我們的成功取決於第三方物流供應商及第三方配送設施。
我們可能無法執行我們的戰略優先事項，這可能會限制我們對業務進行投資及成長的能力。
我們可能無法實現我們在DTC業務運作上的固定成本投資回報。
我們依賴某些舊有資訊科技系統，這些系統可能妨礙我們運作的效率。
我們的成功取決於我們智慧財產權的保護。
我們某些產品受產品規範及/或附帶保固，若未符合規範及/或有保固聲請，可能會導致我們費用增加。
我們可能產生額外稅務負擔，或面臨有效稅率波動。
全球規範及總體經濟與政治情勢，以及潛在的規範、法律及政府政策變動，可能對我們業務產生負面影響。
通貨膨脹與貨幣兌換率波動可能導致營收減少、成本增加及/或邊際利益與獲利下降。
我們管理固定成本的能力，於受季節性影響的業務中，可能影響我們的獲利。
勞動議題、勞動法規變動及我們滿足勞動需求的能力，可能減少我們的營收與獲利。
我們可能因全球市場走弱而產生額外費用、無法取得融資，或無法符合我們融資協議中的財務約束條款。
收購行為面臨許多風險。
極端天氣狀況、氣候變遷及自然災害可能對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生負面影響。
疾病爆發或其他公共衛生威脅，例如大流行病，可能對我們的業務、營運成果與財務狀況產生負面影響。
我們的投資證券可能因市場狀況而受到不利影響。
我們依賴某些關鍵人員。
我們已實施共享服務模式。
我們將專利權授權予第三方，若我們未能選擇適當的授權對象，可能對我們的品牌造成聲譽損害。
本公司普通股價格可能波動。
部分股東持有大量股份，可對本公司施加控制，並能影響公司重大事項。
paragraphs: 除本年度報告表 10-K 所包含的其他資訊外，請謹慎考量下列風險因素，以評估本公司業務。本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流可能因這些及其他風險而受到重大不利影響。請注意，除本公司目前未知或認為不重要之外，可能還有其他風險，也可能影響本公司業務與營運。
本公司進口產品受關稅、進口限制或進口限制等影響，影響各種商品進口至美國及其他市場的成本與數量。美國全球貿易政策的變動，以及未來關稅或其他替代措施或先前追加關稅退款的持續不確定性，已對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生並可能繼續產生負面影響，且可能（在許多情況下已）：
•導致消費者因厭煩通貨膨脹壓力而減少非必要開支，特別是在美國，服飾與鞋類產品價格上漲（請參閱「我們面臨許多可能對消費者及/或批發客戶對我們產品的需求產生負面影響的風險，並導致銷售額及/或獲利下降」）；
•影響我們部分批發客戶的財務狀況（請參閱「我們面臨許多可能對消費者及/或批發客戶對我們產品的需求產生負面影響的風險，並導致銷售額及/或獲利下降」）；
•導致需求與供應之間的不匹配，如我們在 Fall 2025 和 Spring 2026 紅外季節前取消產品訂單所發生的情況（請參閱「我們無法準確預測消費者及/或客戶對我們產品的需求，可能導致存貨積壓或存貨不足，並影響我們的毛利率」）；
•影響全球經濟狀況，並可能導致經濟減速（請參閱「我們面臨許多可能對消費者及/或批發客戶對我們產品的需求產生負面影響的風險，並導致銷售額及/或獲利下降」以及「我們可能產生額外費用、無法取得融資，或無法符合融資協議的財務契約條件，因全球市場走弱」）
